title: Protective Effect of Santonin Against Doxorubicin Induced Cardiotoxicity via TLR4/NF-kappaB, Nrf2/HO-1, and Caspase-3 Pathway Modulation in Rats.
authors: Rehman, Ayema; Abid, Muhammad; Rafique, Zubaria; Khan, Jehan Zeb; Waqas, Muhammad; Haq, Ihsan Ul; Tipu, Muhammad Khalid; Fatima, Humaira; Irshad, Nadeem
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究山道年对阿霉素诱导心脏毒性的保护作用，涉及分子对接但核心为药理实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a potential chemotherapeutic drug, but its practical use is limited as it causes dose-dependent cardiotoxicity. This study aims to explore the cardioprotective role and mechanism of Santonin (Sant) against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity. Initially, Sant's pharmacokinetics, toxicity, and molecular docking with target proteins were determined computationally. In an in vivo study, Sant pretreatment (30 mg/kg and 60 mg/kg) was administered daily via per oral (PO) route, and cardiotoxicity was induced in rats by a single intraperitoneal (IP) injection of DOX (15 mg/kg). The results revealed that Sant demonstrates favorable pharmacokinetics and low toxicity; therefore, it can be administered orally. Moreover, molecular docking studies revealed a significant interaction of Sant with target proteins. Sant pretreatment significantly recovered DOX-induced neurobehavioral changes, body weight changes, relative heart weight, serum cardiac biomarker levels (LDH, CK-MB, Trop I), serum electrolyte levels (Na(+), K(+), Cl(-)), and oxidative stress by modulation of antioxidant and oxidative stress markers levels. Sant improved histopathological alterations and cardiac fibrosis. In addition, Sant downregulates inflammatory mediators such as TLR4 and NF-kappaB, upregulates oxidative stress sensors such as Nrf2 and HO-1, downregulates caspase-3 apoptotic marker, and reverses the DOX-induced DNA damage in cardiac tissue. Sant also decreases the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNF-alpha and IL-1beta in DOX-treated rats. This study suggests for the first time that Sant can prove to be the potential therapeutic option for mitigating DOX-induced cardiotoxicity via modulation of inflammatory (TLR4/NF-kappaB), oxidative stress (Nrf2/HO-1), and apoptotic (Caspase-3) signaling pathways.
abstract_zh: 阿霉素（DOX）是一种潜在的化疗药物，但其实际应用受到剂量依赖性心脏毒性的限制。本研究旨在探讨山道年（Sant）对阿霉素诱导的心脏毒性的心脏保护作用及其机制。首先，通过计算方法确定了Sant的药代动力学、毒性及其与靶蛋白的分子对接。在体内研究中，通过口服（PO）途径每日给予Sant预处理（30 mg/kg和60 mg/kg），并通过单次腹腔注射（IP）DOX（15 mg/kg）诱导大鼠心脏毒性。结果显示，Sant表现出良好的药代动力学特性和低毒性，因此可口服给药。此外，分子对接研究揭示了Sant与靶蛋白的显著相互作用。Sant预处理显著恢复了DOX诱导的神经行为变化、体重变化、相对心脏重量、血清心脏生物标志物水平（LDH、CK-MB、Trop I）、血清电解质水平（Na(+)、K(+)、Cl(-)）以及通过调节抗氧化和氧化应激标志物水平改善的氧化应激。Sant改善了组织病理学改变和心脏纤维化。此外，Sant下调炎症介质如TLR4和NF-kappaB，上调氧化应激传感器如Nrf2和HO-1，下调caspase-3凋亡标志物，并逆转DOX诱导的心脏组织DNA损伤。Sant还降低了DOX处理大鼠中促炎细胞因子如TNF-alpha和IL-1beta的水平。本研究首次表明，Sant可能通过调节炎症（TLR4/NF-kappaB）、氧化应激（Nrf2/HO-1）和凋亡（Caspase-3）信号通路，成为减轻DOX诱导心脏毒性的潜在治疗选择。
